ledger.note: 388: Zhai Liao takes the title of Heavenly King and moves to Huatai. 'In 388, he sent an envoy to Murong Chui to apologize for his crimes'; Chui refused and Zhai Liao 'adopted Chinese tradition, went on the throne', titled Heavenly King, 'moved the capital to Huatai' (Zhai Liao page); infobox 'Established 388'.

zones.text: Liyang and Huatai ('in modern Anyang, Henan', Zhai Liao page): Zhai Liao took Liyang in 386 and made Huatai his capital in 388; drawn as a 55 km disc round Hua County

wars.outcome: Zhai Liao was beaten in late 384, forced to submit in 387, rebelled again in winter 387 and was crushed by Murong Chui in 392 at Liyang.
wars.note: Chui created him Duke of Henan in 387; Zhai Liao attacked Later Yan's Qinghe (roughly Xingtai) that winter.

wars.name: Jin campaign against Zhai Wei
wars.outcome: Zhai Liao took Yingyang in 389 and failed to take Luoyang in 390; the Jin general Liu Laozhi 'captured Juancheng and defeated Zhai Liao near Huatai' in autumn 390 without destroying the state.
wars.note: Zones empty: no page says which side held Juancheng afterward.

certainty.note: A four-year warlord kingdom: commanderies named, no boundary on any page.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; slug zhai-wei, the counterpart later-yan's ledger (gain 392) already uses. Zhai Wei is not in polities.csv. 'Central and eastern Henan' is not on either page: the pages name only Liyang, Huatai, Yingyang (and Qinghe and Pingyuan as Later Yan's). Pre-state: 384-387 (defeat by Murong Lin and Murong Nong, Liyang 386, Duke of Henan 387). The western-jin dossier's 390 and 394 shapes ('276 cells of Hebei and Henan') overlap this country; Cliopatria draws it as Jin land. Unsettled: the 390 Jin counterattack (Juancheng), the 391 attack on Ye by Zhai Zhao (failed), the ending month, Huatai versus Liyang as the main seat.
